def-fermionic-fock-space-over-hilbert-sp:
## Definition

Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. For each $k\ge0$, let $\Lambda^kH$ be the Hilbert exterior power with the Gram-determinant inner product and wedge convention of [[def-hilbert-exterior-power-and-induced-operator]], with $\Lambda^0H=\mathbb C$. The **fermionic Fock space** over $H$ is the Hilbert completion of the algebraic direct sum $\bigoplus_{k\ge0}^{\mathrm{alg}}\Lambda^kH$, where distinct particle-number summands are orthogonal and the inner product on a finite sum is the sum of the inner products of its components. The **vacuum vector** $\Omega$ is $1\in\Lambda^0H$.

On finite sums of decomposable wedges define the creation rule $C(f)\xi=f\wedge\xi$ for $f\in H$. This rule is initially defined on a dense subspace. Its bounded extension and the CAR relations for $C(f)$ and its Hilbert-space adjoint are proved in [[lem-fock-creation-annihilation-satisfy-car]].
def-finite-mode-car-algebra:
## Definition

Fix an integer $n\ge0$. Let $F_n$ be the complex vector space with basis all finite words in the symbols $a_1,\ldots,a_n,a_1^\dagger,\ldots,a_n^\dagger$, including the empty word $1$. Give $F_n$ concatenation as multiplication and the conjugate-linear involution that reverses each word and exchanges $a_j$ with $a_j^\dagger$. Thus $F_n$ is the free unital complex $*$-algebra on $a_1,\ldots,a_n$.

For $x,y$ in an algebra write $\{x,y\}=xy+yx$. Let $J_n$ be the smallest two-sided $*$-ideal in $F_n$ containing

$$ \{a_i,a_j\},\qquad \{a_i^\dagger,a_j^\dagger\},\qquad \{a_i,a_j^\dagger\}-\delta_{ij}1\qquad(1\le i,j\le n). $$

Here a two-sided $*$-ideal is a complex linear subspace closed under left and right multiplication and under $*$. It exists as the intersection of all such ideals containing these relations; the collection is nonempty because it contains $F_n$. The relations are $*$-stable, since taking adjoints exchanges the first two families and changes the third relation with indices $i,j$ to the same relation with indices $j,i$. Define the **algebraic finite-mode CAR $*$-algebra** by $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}_n=F_n/J_n$, with generators denoted by the same symbols. Its quotient map gives the universal property: every tuple in a unital complex $*$-algebra satisfying these relations induces a unique unital $*$-homomorphism from $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}_n$. For $n=0$ there are no generators or relations and $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}_0=\mathbb C$.

This definition is algebraic; the finite-mode universal C*-completion is identified in [[thm-finite-mode-car-algebra-is-full-matrix-algebra]].
thm-square-summable-families-form-a-hilb:
## Statement

For every set $I$, the complex square-summable family space $\ell^2(I,\mathbb C)$ with its canonical norm and inner product from [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]] is complete. Thus it is a complex Hilbert space. Its finitely supported families are dense, and the coordinate vectors form an orthonormal basis. This result uses no choice principle.
def-finite-dimensional-car-algebra:
## Definition

Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the pairing linear in its first variable and conjugate-linear in its second. The **algebraic CAR $*$-algebra over $F$**, denoted $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}(F)$, is generated by symbols $c(f)$, one for each $f\in F$, subject to complex linearity in $f$ and the relations

$$ \{c(f),c(g)\}=0,\qquad \{c(f)^*,c(g)^*\}=0,\qquad \{c(f)^*,c(g)\}=\langle g,f\rangle 1 \quad(f,g\in F), $$

where $\{x,y\}=xy+yx$. Precisely, take the free unital complex $*$-algebra on symbols $c(f)$, with formal adjoints, and quotient by the two-sided $*$-ideal generated by these relations and the linearity relations. The quotient has the universal property that every complex-linear family $C(f)$ in a unital complex $*$-algebra satisfying the displayed relations induces a unique unital $*$-homomorphism from $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}(F)$.

If $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ is an orthonormal basis of $F$, the elements $a_j:=c(e_j)^*$ and $a_j^\dagger:=c(e_j)$ satisfy the finite-mode relations of [[def-finite-mode-car-algebra]]. The algebraic definition does not choose a basis; its finite-dimensional matrix realization is established in [[thm-finite-dimensional-car-algebra-is-matrix-algebra]].
lem-finite-mode-car-occupation-matrix-un:
## Statement

For $n\ge0$, let $\mathcal P_n$ be the set of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathcal F_n=\ell^2(\mathcal P_n)$ with orthonormal basis $e_S$ for $S\in\mathcal P_n$. For $1\le j\le n$ define operators on this finite-dimensional Hilbert space by

$$ c_j e_S=\begin{cases}0&j\notin S,\\(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s<j\}|}e_{S\setminus\{j\}}&j\in S,\end{cases}\qquad c_j^\dagger e_S=\begin{cases}(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s<j\}|}e_{S\cup\{j\}}&j\notin S,\\0&j\in S.\end{cases} $$

Then $c_j^\dagger$ is the Hilbert-space adjoint of $c_j$, and $a_j\mapsto c_j$, $a_j^\dagger\mapsto c_j^\dagger$ defines a $*$-representation $\pi_n:\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}_n\to\operatorname{End}(\mathcal F_n)$. Put $N_j=c_j^\dagger c_j$ and $P_\varnothing=\prod_{j=1}^n(I-N_j)$, with the empty product equal to $I$. For $S=\{i_1<\cdots<i_p\}$ and $T=\{j_1<\cdots<j_q\}$, set

$$ E_{S,T}=c_{i_1}^\dagger\cdots c_{i_p}^\dagger P_\varnothing c_{j_q}\cdots c_{j_1}, $$

with empty operator products equal to $I$. Then $E_{S,T}e_U=\delta_{T,U}e_S$. Consequently the image of $\pi_n$ is all of $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal F_n)\cong M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$.
lem-fock-creation-annihilation-satisfy-c:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first variable, and let $\mathcal F_-(H)$ be its fermionic Fock space. The creation rule $C(f)\xi=f\wedge\xi$ extends to a bounded operator on $\mathcal F_-(H)$ with $\|C(f)\|=\|f\|$. Writing $A(f)=C(f)^*$ for its adjoint, one has, for all $f,g\in H$,

$$ \{C(f),C(g)\}=0,\qquad \{A(f),A(g)\}=0,\qquad \{A(f),C(g)\}=\langle g,f\rangle I. $$

Thus $f\mapsto C(f)$ is a bounded complex-linear CAR family in the convention of [[def-finite-dimensional-car-algebra]].
thm-finite-mode-car-clifford-majorana-is:
## Statement

Let $n\ge0$, let $V=\mathbb C^{2n}$ with ordered basis $e_1,\ldots,e_{2n}$, and put $Q(\sum_r z_re_r)=\sum_r z_r^2$. Use the plus-$Q$ convention of [[def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space]]. Give $\mathrm{Cl}^+(V,Q)$ the conjugate-linear anti-involution that fixes each $e_r$; it is defined by conjugating coefficients, reversing words, and fixing the basis generators. Then there is a $*$-isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{Cl}^+(V,Q)\cong\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}_n $$

specified by

$$ e_{2j-1}\longmapsto \gamma_{2j-1}=a_j+a_j^\dagger,\qquad e_{2j}\longmapsto \gamma_{2j}=i(a_j^\dagger-a_j). $$

The inverse sends $a_j$ to $(e_{2j-1}+ie_{2j})/2$ and $a_j^\dagger$ to $(e_{2j-1}-ie_{2j})/2$. These are finite-mode algebra maps; they assert no relation between CAR and CCR.
thm-finite-mode-car-algebra-is-full-matr:
## Statement

For every integer $n\ge0$, the universal finite-mode CAR $*$-algebra $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}_n$ of [[def-finite-mode-car-algebra]] is $*$-isomorphic to $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal F_n)\cong M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ under the occupation representation of [[lem-finite-mode-car-occupation-matrix-units]], where $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal F_n)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms under composition. Give this matrix algebra the operator norm and conjugate-transpose involution; it is a C*-algebra in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. Every unital $*$-representation on a nonzero Hilbert space is unitarily identified with the matrix action on the occupation coordinate tensored with the identity on one Hilbert space, and is therefore isometric. Consequently the universal C*-norm, the supremum of operator norms over these representations, equals the matrix norm, so the universal C*-completion is the same full matrix algebra.
lem-finite-mode-car-canonical-inclusions:
## Statement

For $n\ge0$, let $\iota_n:\mathsf{CAR}_n\to\mathsf{CAR}_{n+1}$ be the unique unital $*$-homomorphism sending each of the first $n$ annihilation and creation generators to the generator with the same index. Here $\mathsf{CAR}_n$ is the universal finite-mode C*-algebra of [[thm-finite-mode-car-algebra-is-full-matrix-algebra]]. Then $\iota_n$ is isometric and injective. Under the occupation-basis identifications $\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n\otimes\mathbb C^2$, it is represented by $A\mapsto A\otimes I_2$.
thm-finite-dimensional-car-algebra-is-ma:
## Statement

Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension $n$, and let $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}(F)$ be the algebra of [[def-finite-dimensional-car-algebra]]. For any orthonormal basis of $F$, the assignment to the $n$ standard finite-mode annihilation and creation generators identifies $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}(F)$ with $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}_n$. It therefore has a unique finite-dimensional universal C*-norm, and its completion is $*$-isomorphic to $M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$. Every unital $*$-representation of this completion on a nonzero Hilbert space is isometric.
def-countable-mode-car-algebra:
## Definition

Let $\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}$ be the countable mode set. For each $n$ take the universal finite-mode C*-algebra $\mathsf{CAR}_n$ whose dense algebraic presentation is [[def-finite-mode-car-algebra]]. Identify each stage with its image in the next under the isometric inclusion of [[lem-finite-mode-car-canonical-inclusions-are-isometric]]. The inclusions are compatible, injective, and preserve the C*-norm. Their union $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathrm{loc}}=\bigcup_{n\ge0}\mathsf{CAR}_n$ is therefore a normed $*$-algebra with norm $\|x\|=\|x\|_{\mathsf{CAR}_n}$ whenever $x\in\mathsf{CAR}_n$; isometry makes this independent of the stage. Define the **countably infinite-mode CAR C*-algebra** $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathbb N}$ to be the norm completion of $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. Its canonical generator $a_j$ is the image of the $j$th finite-mode generator in any stage $n\ge j$. The C*-axioms pass to the completion because each finite stage satisfies them and multiplication and involution are continuous. The universal property of this inductive-limit construction is proved in [[thm-countable-mode-car-has-universal-inductive-limit-norm]].
lem-car-finite-subspace-inclusions-are-i:
## Statement

If $F\subseteq G$ are finite-dimensional complex inner-product subspaces of a Hilbert space $H$, the generator-preserving map $\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}(F)\to\mathsf{CAR}^{\mathrm{alg}}(G)$ extends to an isometric unital $*$-homomorphism between their finite-dimensional C*-completions.
def-car-algebra-over-hilbert-space:
## Definition

Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. Order its finite-dimensional complex subspaces by inclusion. This is a directed system because the span $F+G$ of any two finite-dimensional subspaces is finite-dimensional. To each such $F$, assign the finite-dimensional CAR C*-algebra of [[thm-finite-dimensional-car-algebra-is-matrix-algebra]], with the generator-preserving maps of [[lem-car-finite-subspace-inclusions-are-isometric]]. Identify each stage with its image under these injective maps and let $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$ be their algebraic union.

The common finite-stage norm is well defined on this union because every inclusion is isometric. Define the **CAR C*-algebra over $H$**, $\mathsf{CAR}(H)$, to be the norm completion of $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$. Addition, multiplication, scalar multiplication, and involution are the compatible finite-stage operations; their norm continuity makes them extend to the completion, and the C*-identity passes to limits. The identity is nonzero because the zero-dimensional stage is $\mathbb C$ and every inclusion preserves its unit. For $f\in H$, write $c(f)$ for the image of the generator in the stage $\operatorname{span}\{f\}$; the universal inductive-limit property and its norm are proved in [[thm-general-car-has-universal-inductive-limit-norm]].
lem-countable-mode-car-particle-hole-aut:
## Statement

There is a unique $*$-automorphism $\alpha$ of $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathbb N}$ satisfying

$$ \alpha(a_j)=a_j^\dagger,\qquad \alpha(a_j^\dagger)=a_j\qquad(j\in\mathbb N). $$

It is involutive: $\alpha^2=I$.
thm-countable-mode-car-has-universal-ind:
## Statement

Let $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathbb N}$ be the inductive-limit C*-algebra of [[def-countable-mode-car-algebra]]. A bounded CAR representation on a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$ means a sequence of bounded linear operators $T_j$ together with specified bounded adjoints $T_j^*$, in the sense of [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], satisfying

$$ \{T_i,T_j\}=0,\qquad \{T_i^*,T_j^*\}=0,\qquad \{T_i,T_j^*\}=\delta_{ij}I_H\qquad(i,j\in\mathbb N). $$

For every such representation there is a unique contractive unital $*$-homomorphism $\rho:\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathbb N}\to\mathcal B(H)$ with $\rho(a_j)=T_j$. The inductive-limit norm on the algebraic union $\mathsf{CAR}_0$ equals the universal norm

$$ \|x\|_{\mathrm u}=\sup_\rho\|\rho(x)\|,\qquad x\in\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathrm{loc}}, $$

where the supremum is over these representations. The norm is finite and the family of representations is nonempty; a concrete representation is the occupation-space representation on $\ell^2(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb N))$ constructed in the proof. Its coordinate vectors $e_S$ form an orthonormal basis, so finite-support vectors are dense.
lem-countable-mode-car-fock-representati:
## Statement

Let $\pi_F$ be the countable-mode occupation representation of $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathbb N}$ on $\mathcal F_\infty=\ell^2(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb N))$ constructed in [[thm-countable-mode-car-has-universal-inductive-limit-norm]]. Then $\pi_F$ is irreducible: its only closed invariant subspaces are $\{0\}$ and $\mathcal F_\infty$. In addition, the common kernel of all annihilators $c_j$ is the vacuum line $\mathbb C e_\varnothing$, whereas the common kernel of all creators $c_j^\dagger$ is $\{0\}$.
thm-general-car-has-universal-inductive-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $\mathsf{CAR}(H)$ be the completion of its directed union of finite-dimensional CAR algebras from [[def-car-algebra-over-hilbert-space]]. Let $K\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $C:H\to\mathcal B(K)$ be a complex-linear family of bounded operators satisfying

$$ \{C(f),C(g)\}=0,\qquad \{C(f)^*,C(g)^*\}=0,\qquad \{C(f)^*,C(g)\}=\langle g,f\rangle I_K \quad(f,g\in H). $$

There is a unique unital isometric $*$-homomorphism $\rho:\mathsf{CAR}(H)\to\mathcal B(K)$ with $\rho(c(f))=C(f)$. For each $x$ in the algebraic union, its inductive-limit norm equals the supremum of $\|\rho(x)\|$ over all such families on nonzero Hilbert spaces. This family is nonempty: the fermionic Fock representation $C(f)\mapsto C(f)$ of [[lem-fock-creation-annihilation-satisfy-car]] attains the norm on every finite stage.
thm-countable-mode-car-has-inequivalent-:
## Statement

Let $\pi_F$ be the countable-mode occupation representation on $\mathcal F_\infty$ and let $\alpha$ be the particle-hole automorphism of [[lem-countable-mode-car-particle-hole-automorphism]]. Then $\pi_F$ and $\pi_{\mathrm h}:=\pi_F\circ\alpha$ are irreducible representations of $\mathsf{CAR}_{\mathbb N}$, and they are not unitarily equivalent. Here two representations are unitarily equivalent if a unitary operator between their Hilbert spaces intertwines their actions. This proves existence of inequivalent irreducible representations; it does not classify all representations.
